### 9. Conduct Root Cause Analysis on Repeated Issues

When a problem shows up often, look deeper than the surface. Root Cause Analysis (RCA) helps you find the true source of recurring issues. [...] The 80/20 rule suggests that 80% of quality issues usually come from 20% of the main causes. This helps teams focus their improvement efforts where they will have the biggest impact.

### What is the complete quality assurance process in a call center?

The QA process includes setting standards, monitoring interactions, scoring performance, giving feedback, and making improvements. These steps help teams maintain consistent and high-quality service. [...] Companies that provide strong customer experiences earn 4–8% more revenue than competitors. Listening closely to your customers helps your team raise service quality and business results.

### 7. Select the Right Sample Size for Call Reviews

Reviewing too many calls wastes time, but reviewing too few hides important trends. Choose a sample size that gives a clear picture of performance without overwhelming your QA team.

Manual QA relies on sampling — reviewing a small percentage of interactions and extrapolating.

Indicators — identified under the Call Outs section — are customizable keywords or phrases that are highlighted within a conversation's analysis. Indicators can be used to capture critical moments of a conversation or track mentions of a specific competitor, feature, product, or phrase. Accounts can use indicators to identify specific elements of conversation that are worth reviewing or tracking. [...] In a contact center context, QA is the ongoing program — scorecards, evaluations, coaching cycles, and trend analysis. QC might refer to a compliance audit, a specific interaction review triggered by a customer complaint, or a post-hoc check on a particular agent's recent calls. Strong contact center operations use both: QA to continuously raise the baseline, and QC to investigate specific failures and prevent recurrence.
